name: Data and inference
description: Summaries of data, samples, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, regression and ANOVA, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about: Data and inference realm ("Data and inference"): summaries of data, samples, estimates, tests and the straight-line model, for an adult who has finished Foundations and Probability and nothing more. Same Kepler outpost, where the records now pile up and Mira wants every decision backed by evidence. The concept plan is docs/plans/STATS-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Describing data
chapters.blurb: Frequency tables, mean, median, mode, quartiles, box plots and outliers.

sector.name: Records Office
sector.purpose: turn a pile of readings into a few honest numbers

chapters.name: Spread and sampling
chapters.blurb: Standard deviation of data, skew, fair samples and the standard error.

sector.name: Survey Camp
sector.purpose: choose fair samples and say how much they vary

chapters.name: Estimating with confidence
chapters.blurb: Confidence intervals for a mean and a proportion, with z and with t.

sector.name: Assay Lab
sector.purpose: say how sure we are about the grade of the ore

chapters.name: Testing a claim
chapters.blurb: Hypotheses, errors, test statistics, p-values and decisions.

sector.name: Inspection Hall
sector.purpose: decide whether a supplier's claim holds up

chapters.name: Comparing groups
chapters.blurb: Two means, two proportions, paired data and chi-square tests.

sector.name: Trial Fields
sector.purpose: tell whether a new seed really beats the old one

chapters.name: Relationships
chapters.blurb: Scatter plots, correlation, the least-squares line and prediction.

sector.name: Solar Farm
sector.purpose: predict the power output from the hours of sunlight

chapters.name: Many groups and the right test
chapters.blurb: Analysis of variance, a test of spread, and choosing the right test.

sector.name: Council Chamber
sector.purpose: back every outpost decision with the right test

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. The records are piling up, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have what this needs from Probability. The only new habit is to ask what a sample can really tell us. I’ll go through the worked example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeTitle:
The records are piling up.
Learn what they really say.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome back. Every dome files readings now, and the council keeps arguing about what they mean. We start with one log and one table; everything you need you learned in Probability.
copy.allDone: You did it. Every outpost decision now rests on evidence you can defend. Logic and proof is next, if you want to know why a conclusion must follow.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from data tables to hypothesis tests and regression. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the result before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Data, read honestly.
help.intro: Data and inference starts where Probability ends. It teaches how to summarise a data set, how a sample stands in for a population, and how to test a claim against it. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: A decision is 1 (reject H₀) or 0; a tail is 1, 2 or 3; a choice of test or interval is the number from the list in the prompt.
